text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- In a surprise move, one of Singapore's most severe critics during the recent row with Malaysia, Umno Youth chief Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, offers an apology to Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew for harsh remarks made about the Singapore leader.
- Taiwan says it has no plans to cancel what it called routine military drills on the eve of Hong Kong's handover, despite a U.S. request not to hold the exercises.
- Visiting senior executive of Canadian telecommunication giant Northern Telecom stabbed during a robbery at Bukit Timah bungalow.
- American communications firm WorldCom Inc, world's largest Internet service provider, says it is confident of clinching next basic telephone licence in Singapore despite stiff competition.
- Singapore Telecom may "have a chance" of buying a stake in Communications Authority of Thailand (CAT), says director of telecommunications planning Phisal Jorphochaudom.
- Government investment arm Temasek Holdings buys 20 percent stake in joint venture developing US$110 million office and retail building in Shanghai's prime HuangPu district.

- Japan will unveil blueprint for its much-touted "Big Bang" financial reforms on Friday, but some experts wonder if nation's financial firms have right stuff to become world-class competitors any time soon.
- Sales of 99-year leasehold landed homes picking up steam, fuelled by competitive pricing and "value for money" factor.
- Growth Triangle linking Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore as an economic sub-region of ASEAN take step forward with inclusion of new areas and signing of eight business deals by private sector.
- Japan's "Mr Yen" proves he still has power to move currency markets by declaring Japan would act decisively against excessive shifts in currency values.

- First state-owned Chinese enterprise to seek primary listing in Singapore, Tianjin Zhong Xin Pharmaceuticals Group, puts up for sale 100 million new shares at 68 US cents each in mainboard initial public offer.
- Jack Chia-MPH Ltd's net earnings fall 16 percent to Singapore $25.4 million for year ended March 31, despite 19 percent rise in turnover to Singapore $684.5 million.
- Thakral Corp stock surges to new year-high of US$1.12 before closing seven cents up at US$1.08 -- thanks to better-than-expected earnings and analysts' bullishness over its outlook.

- Fresh from submitting aggressive bids for two prime leasehold sites at Draycott Drive and Newton Road in land tender, Wing Tai Holdings proposes to raise up to US$200 million through an issue of redeemable convertible cumulative preference shares (RCCPS) of US$1 each.
